mathematical_review: For this recorded axis, minX=244.66666666666666 and maxX=288.66666666666663. Their subtraction is exactly representable (also within Sterbenz ratio bounds); Fraction arithmetic independently confirms it equals the recorded width. Thus the shortfall comes from coordinate endpoint representation rather than additional subtraction rounding.

If each true endpoint is rounded once to nearest, its error is at most half the spacing at that stored endpoint. Their error sum is bounded by max(endpoint ULPs). Here the maximum is5.684341886080802e-14; shortfall is2.842170943040401e-14; adjusted width is44.00000000000003. This is adequate for the observed coordinate subtraction.

This is not a universal bound for arbitrary prior transforms plus another inexact subtraction. A rational counterexample with rounded endpoints-22 and22.000000000000004 yields difference44 with combined endpoint/subtraction error7.034373084024992e-15, greater than max endpoint ULP3.552713678800501e-15. That counterexample does not produce a failing44-threshold decision. The helper should be understood as a tightly bounded UI representation allowance, not a proof of every possible coordinate computation.

No numeric allowance can distinguish true undersizing smaller than that allowance from representation noise. The implementation preserves the meaningful44-point requirement at actual screen-coordinate precision; it does not prove the exact real-number size before all upstream rounding.
implementation_review: Final helper asserts exact44 for each width/height after adding its own axis maximum endpoint ULP. There is no screen-scale rounding, pixel/point margin, changed expected size or changed input frame. It fails finite/nonempty checks before arithmetic.

The separate max(widthRoundoff,heightRoundoff)<1e-9 assertion rejects coarse large-origin representations, including origin2^52/width43 and origin1e18/width0. An assertion records failure even if a caller continues after failure. The1e-9 value is a cap on permitted ULP precision, not an added allowance.

Negative finite origins work because their ULP magnitude is positive. CGRect standardizes negative raw dimensions: size.width=-44 has geometric width44 and is accepted. The helper checks CGRect geometric extents rather than raw size signs; no invalid or undersized app-controlled frame is established by that behavior. Nonfinite origins, infinite dimensions and finite-origin endpoint overflow are rejected.

AX control() still records raw snapshot frames and independently checks labels, enabledness, hittability and complete viewport containment. Failure messages include unmodified frames. Shared room callers retain field entry, Set, keyboard dismissal and functional checks. The guide changes from four cross-axis endpoint ULPs to one per-axis endpoint ULP, a stricter bound.
